title: Lifecycle event (v1)
description: Field set per the-plan §5.2.2. Publish events record `version` + `digest`; `commit` remains an optional legacy/reserved field but is not authored by current writers or used for version resolution, because the enclosing SHA exists only after the event is committed. `id@version` derives the Git object from the descriptor's committed history (D-023).

transition.description: Union of every §3.4 transition-table event name, plus `note` (`expired` is fold-computed, never an event).

state.description: Claimed resulting state; informational only, omitted for transition-free kinds (note, broadcast ack) — fold wins on mismatch (§3.5 rule 5).

produced_by.description: Which tool and version produced this event. OPTIONAL, and it stays optional in the schema on purpose: whether it is REQUIRED is decided per space by min_binary_version reaching the release that introduced it (internal/space.ProducerStampFloor), enforced by `validate --ci`, not here — so a space that has not raised its floor is not retroactively invalidated. Written by the write funnel for every event it commits. It records what the producer CLAIMS: the stamp is emitted by the same client the space is distrusting, so it stops a colleague on a stale binary, not forgery.
